summary: Introductory security posture intake between Redwood AE/SE and Orchard Financial team. High-level requirements: SOC2/ISO proofs, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs retention, KMS/BYOK for keys, data residency for EU, and options between Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Agreed to follow up with docs + technical deep dive on KMS and a Dedicated perf trial.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-04-18 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Daniel Park (Redwood AE), Anika Rao (Redwood SE), Mark Hsu (CISO, Orchard), Priya Menon (Platform Ops), James O'Leary (APAC Compliance), Sofia Alvarez (Eng Lead)

[00:00:05] Daniel: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro — I'm Daniel, AE at Redwood, and Anika is our solutions engineer. We're here to run through Orchard's security and hosting constraints so we can recommend the right mode — hosted, dedicated, or private.

[00:00:18] Mark: Thanks Daniel. Appreciate it. We're trying to get a clearer picture on compliance posture — SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and particularly how KMS and BYOK would work. Also retention windows for logs and audit trails.

[00:00:33] Anika: Great, I'll jump in on the technical bits. Quick question — are you primarily evaluating hosted first and then moving to dedicated, or is private deployment required from day one because of regulation?

[00:00:45] Priya: Right now the product teams prefer hosted for speed, but compliance and legal are pushing for either Dedicated or Private because of key management and data residency. So it's a bit of both — we'd like to see hosted for quick POC but need to validate encryption and SSO.

[00:01:02] James: For APAC and EU customers we have strict residency reqs. We also need to be able to show auditors how keys are managed; BYOK is a hard ask.

[00:01:12] Daniel: Understood. At a high level, Redwood Hosted supports encryption at rest and in transit by default, and we offer customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private modes. We can discuss BYOK flow — Anika, want to outline?

[00:01:25] Anika: Sure. So for Dedicated we support a KMS integration pattern where the customer supplies a CMK in their cloud KMS — that key is used to encrypt model checkpoints and storage. In Private deployments, customers can bring HSM-backed keys. For Hosted we have BYOK options but there are more constraints — rotation, and sometimes we do envelope encryption where Redwood holds the data encryption keys encrypted by customer CMK.

[00:01:50] Mark: Sorry, can you repeat the hosted BYOK part? The envelope term — I missed it.

[00:01:55] Anika: Yeah, so envelope encryption means Redwood never sees your plaintext master key. You have a customer master key (CMK) in, say, AWS KMS or GCP KMS. We encrypt per-tenant data keys with your CMK. The per-tenant data key is used for actual object encryption. That gives you the audit trail in your KMS but we still operate the runtime. There's some nuance on key rotation and emergency key access — we can walk through the exact procedures.

[00:02:20] Sofia: And in terms of SSO — we use SAML 2.0 across teams and SCIM for provisioning. How mature is Redwood's SSO for enterprise?

[00:02:28] Daniel: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning today; RBAC is supported via roles and token scopes. You can map SAML groups to RBAC roles. We also have integrations with Okta, Azure AD, and others.

[00:02:40] Priya: Two specifics from our side: 1) we need per-request audit logs for data access and admin actions with retention up to 7 years for certain data types; 2) the ability to export logs to our SIEM — Splunk or Chronicle.

[00:02:55] Anika: We have audit logging on both control plane and data plane events. Logs can be retained by Redwood and also forwarded to your SIEM via secure streaming. The default retention window in Hosted is 90 days, but Dedicated and Private allow longer retention on customer-managed storage. Forwarding to SIEM is standard; we may need to configure log endpoints and authentication.

[00:03:18] James: Are the audit logs tamper-evident? Auditors ask about immutability..

[00:03:22] Anika: Good question. We support write-once log sinks in Private deployments using customer-managed storage buckets with object lock. For Hosted we provide signed log ingestion and append-only streams; we can produce a signed chain of custody report. We'll be transparent about limitations — for the full immutability guarantee we usually recommend Private with object-locked storage.

[00:03:40] Mark: Ok interesting. On SOC 2 — do you have a Type II? And can we get the report?

[00:03:46] Daniel: Yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, and we also publish an ISO 27001 summary. I'll share the report under NDA.

[00:03:53] Mark: Cool. Please do. Also, on network architecture — for Dedicated we'd need VPC peering and private endpoints. Is that supported?

[00:04:02] Anika: Yes. Dedicated supports VPC peering and private link-style connectivity. Private deployment is customer-managed so you get full control over networking. Hosted offers IP allowlisting and private endpoints in some regions for enterprise customers.

[00:04:18] Priya: Latency is a factor. If we go Dedicated in us-east1, what's the expected p95 for small prompt generation? We need p95 < 200ms for token-limited routes.

[00:04:28] Anika: Our benchmarks show sub-150ms p95 on recent Llama-family models with Dedicated GPU pools configured for low-latency. The actual number depends on model, sequence length, and batching. For Hosted we have shared pools — latency is often slightly higher at high load. We can run a perf bench on a trial Dedicated node to confirm.

[00:04:45] Sofia: For the perf bench, can we also test KV cache behavior? We often see cold-start spikes due to KV loads.

[00:04:50] Anika: Yes, we can instrument KV cache hit rates and show how prefix caching reduces cost/latency. We'll include that in the bench.

[00:04:58] James: Back to KMS — the APAC team is worried about key residency. Can we have keys in our Tokyo region KMS and still use Redwood's hosted inference?

[00:05:06] Anika: If keys must stay in region, Hosted becomes trickier. We do have regional hosting options; however, if the CMK cannot leave the customer's control and must be in a customer-managed KMS in Tokyo, Dedicated or Private are the cleaner options. For Hosted, we can sometimes set up a regional instance—needs legal review.

[00:05:24] Mark: Another ask: separation of duties. We need to ensure that our engineers can't access audit logs or KMS keys unless explicitly permitted. How is RBAC implemented?

[00:05:33] Daniel: You can enforce least privilege via RBAC roles in Redwood Console. There are admin, billing, deployer, and viewer roles by default; you can create custom roles. SCIM group sync allows you to map OKTA groups to those roles. For Dedicated/Private you can also enforce network-level restrictions and use your IAM for access control.

[00:05:50] Priya: And what about retention of model inputs? We have PII concerns. We need an option to not persist raw inputs beyond inference time or to redact sensitive tokens.

[00:05:59] Anika: We support configurable retention policies. Hosted defaults to short-lived caches for latency benefits, and you can opt out of data retention entirely in Dedicated/Private. We also offer an automatic PII redaction preprocessor as an opt-in stage for incoming prompts, though it has edge cases.

[00:06:16] Mark: Does Redwood perform any training/learning with customer data?

[00:06:19] Daniel: No. We do not use customer data to update models unless explicitly agreed in a separate contract. We have policies and controls to ensure inference data isn't used for training.

[00:06:26] Sofia: For audits we need a diagram that shows where log generation occurs, what is stored, and what is forwarded. Can you provide that?

[00:06:31] Anika: Absolutely — we'll provide an architecture diagram showing control plane, data plane, where keys live, and log export flows.

[00:06:36] James: One compliance nuance — our privacy team wants to know about deletion guarantees. If a user requests data deletion, can Redwood purge all traces including backups?

[00:06:45] Anika: We have data deletion workflows. In Hosted there's a best-effort for backups; in Dedicated/Private, since you control storage, deletion can be fully controlled. We can provide a deletion certificate for audit trails where feasible. We'll note there are retention windows that legal teams often define.

[00:06:58] Mark: Are you able to provide a list of sub-processors and their SOC status? Auditors want that list.

[00:07:03] Daniel: Yes, we'll send the sub-processor list with SOC statuses. We'll include cloud provider info and any third-party telemetry providers.

[00:07:10] Priya: On the legal side, egress charges and data residency — if we move traffic to EU, how do you handle cross-border requests? We need contractual guarantees on data not leaving EU for certain customer sets.

[00:07:20] Daniel: We can offer regionally pinned deployments for EU customers. For Hosted, we can route EU requests to EU infra and apply data residency filters. For full contractual guarantees, Dedicated/Private is the usual path. We'll work with contracts to add data residency clauses.

[00:07:34] Anika: Quick note: some features like certain BYOK modes require additional entitlements or an enterprise plan. We'll call those out in the doc we send.

[00:07:42] Mark: Budget question — how much more does Dedicated typically cost vs Hosted? We need a ballpark for procurement.

[00:07:47] Daniel: Depends on the committed capacity and GPU type. For predictable throughput, Dedicated usually starts at an additional 2x OPEX compared to pay-as-you-go hosted depending on utilization, but with reserved commits the unit cost can go down heavily. I'll include a few scenarios in the follow-up.

[00:08:03] Sofia: Will the Dedicated nodes be single-tenant? How isolated is the runtime?

[00:08:09] Anika: Dedicated is single-tenant at the GPU level and has tenant isolation in compute and storage. For Private you own the entire stack. There are also soft limits and cgroup-level isolation.

[00:08:20] James: Can you walk us through an incident response example? If a key is potentially compromised, what's the playbook?

[00:08:26] Anika: Sure — short version: 1) rotate the CMK (customer side) and create a new key version; 2) rotate envelope keys and rewrap data keys; 3) revoke access tokens; 4) execute a controlled failover if needed. In Private, you manage keys directly. In Hosted, we coordinate and provide playbooks and support for emergency rotations. We'll include an IR runbook.

[00:08:46] Mark: Good. Another auditor ask — do you provide attestations for pen tests and vulnerability scanning?

[00:08:51] Daniel: We run regular pen tests and scans and will provide summaries/attestation letters; full reports are often shared under NDA.

[00:08:59] Priya: For the perf bench — can we get synthetic traffic that simulates our burst patterns? We have diurnal peaks and heavy batch jobs at night.

[00:09:06] Anika: Yes, send us traces or RPS/sequence length distributions and we'll replay them on the trial node. We'll instrument cost-per-token and latency by percentiles.

[00:09:15] Sofia: One small thing — data classification tags. Can Redwood tag datasets/inputs for retention rules?

[00:09:20] Anika: You can attach metadata to routes and prompts and apply retention policies based on tags in Dedicated/Private. In Hosted it's more limited but we have per-route policies.

[00:09:29] Mark: Anything we should be aware of with respect to regulatory encryption standards — FIPS, etc?

[00:09:34] Anika: For FIPS workloads we recommend Private with FIPS-validated HSMs. Some cloud KMS offerings have FIPS modes; we'll map those to your requirements.

[00:09:44] [00:09:44] (brief crosstalk)

[00:09:46] Daniel: Ok wrapping up next steps: we'll send SOC 2 and ISO docs under NDA, the sub-processor list, an architecture diagram, a KMS/BYOK checklist, and a Dedicated trial proposal for perf tests. We'll aim for the KMS deep dive next Friday.

[00:09:59] Mark: Sounds good. Also we'll send over our retention policy and an example SIEM endpoint for log forwarding.

[00:10:05] Priya: And provisioning — if we go for a trial Dedicated node, what's the lead time?

[00:10:09] Anika: Usually 3-5 business days to provision a trial Dedicated node once the scope is agreed and there's an account for billing. For Private, lead times are longer.

[00:10:17] Sofia: Quick objection from procurement — we need clarity on termination: what happens to keys and data after contract end?

[00:10:23] Daniel: We'll include contractual language. General approach: we return a deletion certificate and help with key rotations and data purge. For BYOK, if keys are in your KMS we can validate that data keys are revoked.

[00:10:33] James: Ok thanks. Anything else from Redwood?

[00:10:36] Anika: Not from me. We'll also highlight any feature flags that require enterprise entitlements, like extended audit retention in Hosted.

[00:10:45] Daniel: Great. We'll follow up with all artifacts and proposed dates. Thanks everyone.

[00:10:50] Mark: Thanks — appreciate it.

Notes: Conversation included typical sales discovery elements — qualification (hosted vs dedicated vs private), compliance evidence requests, technical constraints for KMS/BYOK and key residency, RBAC mapping to SCIM/SAML, audit log retention and forwarding, perf bench requests (latency and KV cache), incident response and deletion guarantees. Next actions and owners captured in action_items.

End of transcript.
